name: Tiramisu
tagline: Espresso-soaked ladyfingers layered with mascarpone cream.

preparation.title: Brew espresso
preparation.description: Espresso is brewed fresh and left to cool completely.

preparation.title: Whip the cream
preparation.description: Egg yolks and sugar are whisked, then folded with mascarpone.

preparation.title: Dip the ladyfingers
preparation.description: Ladyfingers are briefly dipped in espresso, not soaked.

preparation.title: Layer
preparation.description: Alternating layers of soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream.

preparation.title: Chill & dust
preparation.description: Chilled for hours, then dusted with cocoa just before serving.

discover.chefNotes: We dip, never soak, the ladyfingers -- three seconds each side. Any longer and the layers turn to mush by the time it reaches your table.
facts: The name means "pick me up," a reference to the espresso and sugar meant to lift your spirits.
First documented in Treviso restaurants in the 1960s, making it young by Italian dessert standards.
Traditional recipes use raw egg yolks, whisked with sugar over gentle heat for safety.
discover.culturalBackground: Tiramisu's rapid spread from a regional Veneto specialty to Italy's most internationally recognized dessert happened within a single generation, unusually fast for a dish rooted in tradition.
